description:
The maintainer wants a TRANSIENT simulator; steady state is the baseline starting point, not the destination.

UPSTREAM EXISTS — correcting a common assumption: DWSIM is not steady-state-only. DWSIM.DynamicsManager (12 files, 972 lines) carries Integrator.vb, Schedule.vb, Event.vb, EventSet.vb, MonitoredVariable.vb and CauseAndEffectMatrix.vb, and DWSIM.FlowsheetSolver handles dynamic-mode execution. So this is a port with a reference, not a from-scratch design.

SCOPE: the integrator loop and its time stepping, the schedule and event model, monitored variables, and the dynamic-mode branch of the flowsheet execution order. The DynamicsManager itself is a thin orchestration layer — the actual transient behaviour comes from unit operations carrying holdup, which is a separate bead.

Steady-state solve remains the initial condition provider for every transient run.
title: refinery: transient mode — port the DWSIM dynamics integrator and dynamic-mode execution

description:
Observed 2026-08-13 on the Windows 11 clone at C:/Users/fifad/Documents/research/outram-park-backend.

scripts/install-token-hooks.sh sets core.hooksPath=.githooks correctly, but there is no Python interpreter on this machine: python3, python and py all resolve to the Windows Store alias stub ('Python was not found'). .githooks/prepare-commit-msg is deliberately non-blocking (|| true), so commits succeed but carry NO API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit trailer at all -- not even the legitimate total=0 source=none form.

Consequence: commits made from this machine are invisible to docs/historian/token_usage.py query and to the historian report, so any develop->main historian report generated later will under-count this window rather than showing a documented zero.

Affected commits so far: the 'policy: make the working-hours guardrail opt-in per session' commit and the two merge commits on develop from 2026-08-13.

Options for the maintainer:
1. Install Python on the Windows box (simplest; restores the hook).
2. Port the trailer logic to a PowerShell or Rust equivalent so the hooks work toolchain-free.
3. Accept the gap and note Windows-origin commits as untracked in the historian report.

Do not hand-write trailers to paper over this -- CLAUDE.md forbids inventing the numbers.
title: Token-accounting hooks are a no-op on the Windows clone (no Python)

description:
BLOCKS EVERY REACTOR CHILD. reference-data/endf currently holds 12 files: U-235, U-238, H-2, He-4, Ar-37, and thermal-scattering laws for Al-27, C-in-SiC, Si-in-SiC, crystalline graphite, reactor graphite 10P and 30P, and H-in-ZrH.

That is enough for a bare HEU sphere and nothing else in the target set.

MISSING, by reactor:
  every oxide fuel   O-16
  all light water    H-1, and H-in-H2O TSL
  heavy water        D-2 present as H-2; needs D-in-D2O TSL, O-16
  clad / structure   Zr-90..96, Fe-54/56/57/58, Cr, Ni
  control            B-10, B-11, Ag-In-Cd or Hf depending on reactor
  EBR-I / EBR-II     Pu-239/240/241, Na-23, U-234/236, fast-spectrum set
  MSRE               Li-7, Be-9, F-19, Zr, Th-232, U-233
  HTR-10 / HTTR      already have graphite and SiC TSLs; need O-16, B-10

njoy::acquire::EndfCache is the seam and is 'always compiled' per its own docs; the fetch half is feature-gated. Task: drive it to populate the set, record provenance (library and version per nuclide — ENDF/B-VIII.0 vs TENDL matters and the one TENDL file here is already mixed in), and write the inventory into reference-data/endf/README.md.

SIZE WARNING: the current 12 files are 96 MB. A full set for seven reactors is plausibly several GB. Decide whether it is committed, cached, or fetched on demand BEFORE bulk-downloading — this repo should not grow by gigabytes of redistributable evaluated data without that being a deliberate choice.

Parent: op-wpi0
title: Pipeline stage 1: acquire the ENDF nuclides the reactor set actually needs

description:
Observed 2026-08-11 during the librarian pass, kovan CLI built from workspace at target/release/kovan (08:40 build).

REPRODUCTION (actually run):
./target/release/kovan lit import 'kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf' --json-out crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tobias1980decay.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/proprietary/tobias1980decay.md

OBSERVED: the summary printed 'visibility: Open' and the JSON was written with visibility Open — even though both --json-out and --markdown-out point into proprietary/ trees. The path-based visibility inference (storage::visibility_from_path per DECISIONS.md) evidently looks only at the SOURCE path (kovan_import/...), which contains neither open/ nor proprietary/, and the fallback default is Open.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the normal workflow (kovan_import/README.md) imports FROM staging, so every proprietary import gets visibility Open by default. That is the expensive failure direction — DECISIONS.md itself says the design goal was 'proprietary material can't be mislabelled open by accident', and this defeats it. The same run also imported an open document correctly, so only the default is wrong.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: infer visibility from the --json-out destination path when the source path is indeterminate, and/or default to Proprietary (the cheap failure direction) instead of Open, and/or print a loud warning when falling back.

The tobias1980decay.json record was hand-patched to Proprietary the same day; no mislabelled record remains.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-11, pending maintainer verification. Maintainer decision: 'for lit import, visibilty should be closed by default. And open if explicitly stated.'

Implemented in crates/kovan-literature/src/lib.rs, storage::visibility_from_path. A document is now Open ONLY when its path contains an explicit open/ component; everything else, including a path with neither marker, is Proprietary.

WHY THE OLD TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: the existing test asserted exactly two cases, open/papers/x.pdf and proprietary/reports/x.pdf. Both pass under the OLD rule and the NEW one, because neither exercises the unmarked path. The defect lived entirely in the case nobody wrote a test for. The replacement test now covers a bare filename, a kovan_import/ staging path, an absolute Downloads path, case-insensitive OPEN/, and a substring trap (openfoam_cases/ must NOT be read as an open marker). 69 lib tests pass.

Note the ORIGINAL doc comment claimed the function existed 'so proprietary material never gets an open label by accident' — the stated intent was right all along and the implementation contradicted it. Worth remembering as a review heuristic: when a doc comment states a safety property, check the code actually delivers it.

title: kovan-literature: lit import defaults visibility to Open when the source PDF is outside open/ or proprietary/ (staging imports)
